newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends on quiet note, seen to drift.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends on quiet note, seen to drift.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market ended quietly on Thursday with most people sidelined a day after arbitrage-related play perked up the business yesterday, dealers said.

"I think there were some deals done for RSS3 today, but the level of activity was not like yesterday when we saw several houses involved in arbitrage-related activity between the market here and the ones in Japan," a dealer said.
"Yesterday, there was a lot of activity in RSS3 and RSS1. I think some of those deals were just registered today. I've done practically nothing for most of the day," another trader said.
Dealers said most of the players in the market were sidelined and it seems likely prices will probably drift tomorrow ahead of the weekend, dealers said.
"It's pretty quiet. I think the market may be quiet again tomorrow unless Japanese players again gives the local market a push," a dealer said.

At 0945 GMT, August RSS3 was seen at 113.00-114.00 U.S. cents a kg from 113.50 cents. August RSS1 was seen at 161.00-163.00 Singapore cents (US$1.13-$1.14) a kg from 162.00 cents. October/December TSR20 was seen unchanged at 108.50 U.S. cents a kg. - (S$1.42 = US$1) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
